subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The intercepts made on the coordinate axes by the straight line x tanα + y secα = 1 have product sinα. Find α.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 36, book p.146. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark for reading both intercepts off the line and one for solving the trigonometric equation the product condition produces. The answer is authored as the general solution α = (2n + 1)π/4 with the acute value π/4 named, because tan²α = 1 has two families and reporting only 45° drops half of them; both were checked by substitution back into the original line. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how you get each intercept, and what equation the product condition turns into.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both intercepts
steps.margin_note: First mark. An intercept is what is left when the other variable is set to zero, and 1/tan α = cot α, 1/sec α = cos α.
steps.memory_tip: For the x-intercept put y = 0; for the y-intercept put x = 0. Then use 1/tan = cot and 1/sec = cos.
lines: Given line is  x tanα + y secα = 1
Put y = 0:  x tanα = 1  ⇒  x = cotα
Put x = 0:  y secα = 1  ⇒  y = cosα
(tanα ≠ 0 here, so α is not a multiple of π.)

recall.must_convey: That the intercepts are cot α and cos α.
accept: put y equals zero to get x equals cot alpha
put x equals zero to get y equals cos alpha
the intercepts are cot alpha and cos alpha
y ni zero pettina x intercept vasthundi
one over tan is cot and one over sec is cos

steps.why: The line is not written in intercept form, so each intercept has to be read off by setting the other variable to zero; writing them as cot α and cos α keeps the next step in one trigonometric family.
common_mistakes: Giving the intercepts as tan α and sec α, which are the coefficients, not the intercepts.
Setting x = 0 to get the x-intercept.

steps.label: Use the product condition
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cot α · cos α = cos²α/sin α, so the condition becomes cos²α = sin²α, which is cos 2α = 0.
steps.memory_tip: cos²α = sin²α is the same as cos 2α = 0. Its solutions are the odd multiples of π/4.

lines.text: (the product of the two intercepts from step 1)
(multiply both sides by sin α, which is not 0)

recall.must_convey: That the condition reduces to cos 2α = 0, so α = (2n + 1)π/4, with π/4 the acute value.
accept: cot alpha into cos alpha equals sin alpha
cos squared alpha equals sin squared alpha
cos two alpha is zero so alpha is an odd multiple of pi by four
cos two alpha zero ayithe alpha pi by four vasthundi

steps.why: Dividing by sin α is safe because sin α is not zero here: α is not a multiple of π, which the x-intercept already required. cos²α = sin²α is the double-angle form cos 2α = 0, whose solutions are exactly the odd multiples of π/4.
common_mistakes: Cancelling to tan α = 1 only, and losing the tan α = −1 family.
Giving 45° alone without the general value.
